chosen_translation: I enjoy watching football.
rejected_translation: To me it is pleasing to watch football.
defect_description: Dative 'мне нравится' rendered word-for-word; 'I enjoy' required.

chosen_translation: He does sports every morning.
rejected_translation: He is engaged in sport every morning.
defect_description: 'Занимается спортом' = does sports/exercises; 'engaged in sport' is overly formal.

source: Команда забила гол на последней минуте.
chosen_translation: The team scored a goal in the last minute.
rejected_translation: Team struck a goal on last minute.
defect_description: Articles required; 'scored a goal' is the correct collocation; 'on last minute' should be 'in the last minute'.

source: Он бежит марафон уже третий раз.
chosen_translation: He is running a marathon for the third time.
rejected_translation: He runs the marathon already third time.
defect_description: Dative-style rendering; natural English uses present continuous + ordinal with 'for'.

source: Они выиграли чемпионат два года назад.
chosen_translation: They won the championship two years ago.
rejected_translation: They have won the championship two years ago.
defect_description: Specific past time reference 'ago' requires simple past, not present perfect.

chosen_translation: He is a good athlete.
rejected_translation: He is a good sportsman.
defect_description: 'Спортсмен' in modern context translates as athlete; 'sportsman' implies hunting/fishing in British usage.

chosen_translation: The coach is demanding of his players.
rejected_translation: The trainer is demanding to his players.
defect_description: Team sport leader is a 'coach'; 'demanding of' is the correct collocation, not 'demanding to'.

chosen_translation: Don't give up!
rejected_translation: I implore you not to surrender under any circumstances!
defect_description: Motivational cheer uses direct short imperative, not formal plea.

chosen_translation: Play fair!
rejected_translation: I urge you to conduct yourself in an honourable manner during the contest!
defect_description: Sports sportsmanship reminder uses short imperative, not formal admonition.

chosen_translation: The game is not worth the candle.
rejected_translation: The game is not worth candles.
defect_description: Fixed English idiom 'the game is not worth the candle' — singular 'the candle' required.

chosen_translation: The winners are not judged.
rejected_translation: Winners are not being judged.
defect_description: Russian proverb maps to 'might makes right' or 'winners write history'; the literal rendering is unusual.

chosen_translation: He is fighting for first place.
rejected_translation: He struggles for first place.
defect_description: 'Бороться' in competition context is 'fighting for'; 'struggles' implies hardship rather than competition.

chosen_translation: The final takes place on Saturday.
rejected_translation: The final will be taking place on Saturday.
defect_description: Scheduled event uses simple present; progressive form is awkward here.

chosen_translation: The stadium holds fifty thousand spectators.
rejected_translation: The stadium contains fifty thousand spectators.
defect_description: 'Вмещает' for venues means holds/seats; 'contains' implies the spectators are already inside.

chosen_translation: The fans are chanting their player's name.
rejected_translation: The fans scan the name of their player.
defect_description: 'Скандировать' means to chant; 'scan' is a false friend.

source: Он установил рекорд на прошлой неделе.
chosen_translation: He set a record last week.
rejected_translation: He established a record last week.
defect_description: 'Установил рекорд' = set a record; 'established' is non-idiomatic in sports context.

chosen_translation: They won three to one.
rejected_translation: They won with score three–one.
defect_description: Score expressed as 'three to one' without preamble; 'with score' is non-standard.

chosen_translation: The referee sent the player off.
rejected_translation: The judge removed the player from the field.
defect_description: Sports official is a 'referee'; 'sent off' is the correct sporting idiom; 'judge' is a false friend.

source: Концерт прошёл на ура, и все уходили счастливые.
chosen_translation: The concert was a great success, and everyone left happy.
rejected_translation: The concert was a great success.
defect_description: Second clause about audience leaving happily dropped.

source: Несмотря на травму, он продолжил игру.
chosen_translation: Despite the injury, he continued playing.
rejected_translation: He continued playing.
defect_description: Concessive clause 'несмотря на травму' dropped.

chosen_translation: She is into yoga.
rejected_translation: She is fascinated by yoga.
defect_description: 'Увлекаться' for a hobby means to be into something; 'fascinated by' implies intellectual wonder rather than regular practice.

chosen_translation: The film ran for two hours.
rejected_translation: The film went two hours.
defect_description: 'Шёл' for a film's duration means ran for; 'went' is non-standard.

chosen_translation: The play was performed brilliantly.
rejected_translation: The piece was played magnificently.
defect_description: 'Пьеса' in theatre is a play; 'piece' implies music; 'performed' preferred over 'played' for theatre.

chosen_translation: She collects stamps.
rejected_translation: She collections stamps.
defect_description: 'Коллекционирует' is the verb 'collects'; 'collections' is a noun.

source: Он записывает музыку в свободное время.
chosen_translation: He records music in his free time.
rejected_translation: He writes music in free time.
defect_description: 'Записывает музыку' = records music (studio/digital); 'writes' implies composition; 'in his free time' needs possessive.

chosen_translation: The fans supported the team throughout the game.
rejected_translation: The supporters held the team through the game.
defect_description: 'Поддерживали' = supported; 'held' is a mistranslation of the Russian stem.

chosen_translation: The match was postponed due to bad weather.
rejected_translation: The match was transferred due to bad weather.
defect_description: 'Перенесли' in scheduling context means postponed; 'transferred' is the false friend calque.

chosen_translation: He is an artist by vocation.
rejected_translation: He is an artist by calling.
defect_description: 'Призвание' maps more naturally to 'vocation'; 'calling' is a slightly religious variant but acceptable — the better-natural option is 'vocation'.

source: Она посещает театр раз в месяц.
chosen_translation: She goes to the theatre once a month.
rejected_translation: She visits theatre once in a month.
defect_description: 'Once a month' is the correct frequency expression; 'visits theatre' needs definite article.

source: Победа досталась им нелегко, но они заслужили её.
chosen_translation: The victory did not come easily to them, but they deserved it.
rejected_translation: The victory did not come easily to them.
defect_description: Second clause affirming they deserved it dropped.

chosen_translation: He paints in oils.
rejected_translation: He draws by oil.
defect_description: 'Рисует маслом' = paints in oils; 'draws' implies pencil/charcoal; 'by oil' is incorrect preposition.

source: Спектакль длился три часа с антрактом.
chosen_translation: The show ran for three hours including the interval.
rejected_translation: The spectacle lasted three hours with an intermission.
defect_description: 'Спектакль' is a theatrical performance/show not a 'spectacle'; 'антракт' is an interval.

source: Он играет на гитаре уже пять лет.
chosen_translation: He has been playing the guitar for five years.
rejected_translation: He plays guitar already five years.
defect_description: Ongoing activity requires present perfect continuous with 'for' and article before 'guitar'.

chosen_translation: The film is showing at eight in the evening.
rejected_translation: Cinema is showing at eight in the evening.
defect_description: 'Кино' here refers to the film, not the cinema building; 'the film is showing' is correct.

chosen_translation: He played brilliantly.
rejected_translation: He played glitteringly.
defect_description: 'Блестяще' as an adverb means brilliantly; 'glitteringly' is not standard English.

chosen_translation: The artist created the painting in a week.
rejected_translation: The artist created a picture for a week.
defect_description: Completed creation uses 'in a week' (duration to complete); 'for a week' implies ongoing activity.

chosen_translation: He has been passionate about chess since childhood.
rejected_translation: He is fascinated by chess from childhood.
defect_description: Ongoing state from childhood requires present perfect; 'since childhood' not 'from childhood'.

chosen_translation: The team is in good shape.
rejected_translation: The team is in good form.
defect_description: 'Форма' in sport context means form/shape; 'in good shape' is the more natural idiomatic English.

chosen_translation: The exhibition is open until the end of the month.
rejected_translation: The exposition is open till end of month.
defect_description: 'Выставка' is exhibition not exposition; 'till end of month' lacks articles and is informal.

chosen_translation: The audience gave a standing ovation.
rejected_translation: The spectators applauded standing.
defect_description: 'Аплодировали стоя' maps to the English idiom 'standing ovation'.

chosen_translation: He failed the audition.
rejected_translation: He failed the hearing.
defect_description: 'Прослушивание' in performing arts means audition; 'hearing' is a legal/medical false friend.

chosen_translation: The stage was decorated with flowers.
rejected_translation: The scene was decorated with flowers.
defect_description: 'Сцена' in theatre context is the stage; 'scene' is a false friend.

source: Она начала заниматься балетом в шесть лет.
chosen_translation: She started taking ballet lessons at the age of six.
rejected_translation: She began to be occupied with ballet at six years.
defect_description: 'Заниматься балетом' means to take ballet lessons; 'at the age of six' is the correct English expression for age.

chosen_translation: He supports the local team.
rejected_translation: He is sick for the local team.
defect_description: 'Болеть за команду' is a Russian idiom meaning to support/root for; 'sick for' is a false literal rendering.

chosen_translation: The match ended in a draw.
rejected_translation: The match finished in draw.
defect_description: 'Ended in a draw' requires the indefinite article; 'finished in draw' is ungrammatical.

source: Он проявил истинное мастерство в финале, и зрители были в восторге.
chosen_translation: He showed true mastery in the final, and the audience was thrilled.
rejected_translation: He showed true mastery in the final.
defect_description: Second clause about audience reaction dropped.

chosen_translation: A hobby helps relieve stress.
rejected_translation: Hobby helps to remove stress.
defect_description: Indefinite article required before 'hobby'; 'relieve stress' is the correct collocation.

source: Он играл роль злодея в этом спектакле.
chosen_translation: He played the villain in this show.
rejected_translation: He played the role of the villain in this spectacle.
defect_description: 'Играл роль' idiomatically is 'played the villain'; 'spectacle' is a false friend for 'спектакль'.

source: Он не вылезает из тренажёрного зала.
chosen_translation: He practically lives at the gym.
rejected_translation: He doesn't climb out of the fitness hall.
defect_description: 'Не вылезать из тренажёрного зала' idiomatically means to practically live at the gym.

source: После победы команда отпраздновала, и болельщики вышли на улицы.
chosen_translation: After the victory, the team celebrated, and the fans took to the streets.
rejected_translation: After the victory, the team celebrated.
defect_description: Second clause about fans celebrating in the streets dropped.
